headline: Oil crashes nearly 6% as Houthis attack Riyadh and world leaders gather at the UN — ASX barely moved while your US holdings had a mixed last night.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: TTWO had a rough last night, dropping 2.5% with no major company-specific news driving it — just broader market jitters. GTA Online support was confirmed and there's chatter about a new 2027 game mode, so the long-term story around GTA VI remains intact. This looks like noise rather than a structural problem.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS slipped 1.2% today, continuing its tough run — it's now down 38% on your purchase price. Lithium prices remain under pressure globally as EV demand growth has disappointed and supply has surged. No fresh news today, but the macro headwinds for lithium miners aren't going away quickly.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: GXAI had a solid session today, up 1.15% on the ASX, likely riding general optimism around AI stocks. The ETF tracks a basket of global AI-exposed companies, so last night's mild gains on the NASDAQ filtered through here.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE was today's standout on the ASX, up 1.25%. Emerging markets got a lift, possibly from a slightly softer US dollar and improving sentiment around China's economy. A good day for this one.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft slipped 0.8% last night — nothing dramatic. No specific bad news; it looks like routine profit-taking after a strong run. Microsoft's AI and cloud business fundamentals remain as strong as ever.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG ticked up 0.53% today, a quiet but solid session. As a diversified fund spanning Aussie and global shares, it broadly tracked the positive tone across most markets.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS gained 0.53% today on the ASX, reflecting last night's mild gains on US markets. The S&P 500 and NASDAQ both nudged higher, and that's flowing through to this US total market ETF.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: GOOGL edged up 0.21% last night — a quiet session. Google Cloud hit $20B in quarterly revenue but there are some questions around free cash flow. Nothing alarming; the AI-driven cloud growth story is still very much alive.

watch_today.title: TTWO: Hold through the dip
watch_today.detail: Take-Two fell 2.45% last night but there's no bad news — GTA Online support is confirmed and a new 2027 mode is being teased. You're down 11.5% overall but the GTA VI launch catalyst is still ahead of you. For a long-term holder, sit tight.

watch_today.title: PLS: Painful, but hold — don't panic sell
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals is your biggest loser, down 38% on what you paid. Today's 1.2% dip is small in the context of the bigger picture. Lithium prices are still soft and there's no near-term catalyst visible, but selling now locks in the loss. If you believe in the long-term EV transition story, hold. Only reconsider if you need the capital.

watch_today.title: Oil crashes 5.7% — watch the flow-on effects
watch_today.detail: Crude oil (WTI) plunged from ~$102 to ~$96 a barrel last night — a near 6% drop. Houthi attacks on Riyadh caused alarm, but paradoxically markets may be pricing in demand destruction fears overriding supply risk. Cheaper oil is generally good for the broader economy and can ease inflation, which is positive for your diversified holdings like VDHG and VTS.

watch_today.title: RBA rate rise fears — ASX may face more pressure this week
watch_today.detail: Reports are circulating that traders are pricing in three more RBA (Reserve Bank of Australia) rate rises. Higher rates make borrowing more expensive and can drag on share prices, especially growth stocks. Worth watching how the ASX opens Monday — your ASX holdings (VDHG, VGE, VTS, GXAI, PLS) could face headwinds.

watch_today.title: GXAI: Good day, long-term story building
watch_today.detail: Your AI ETF gained 1.15% today and is a natural beneficiary of the ongoing AI boom. Despite being down 11.7% overall, the structural tailwinds behind AI investment are strong. Hold and keep adding if you're dollar-cost averaging.

watch_today.title: VGE: Emerging markets bouncing — hold comfortably
watch_today.detail: VGE jumped 1.25% today — best mover in your ASX portfolio. Emerging markets are showing some life. You're only slightly underwater (-1.5%) so this is a comfortable hold with good long-term diversification value.

world.summary: A big weekend globally — Houthi rebels struck Saudi Arabia's capital, world leaders converged on the UN General Assembly with Ukraine and the Middle East dominating, and California moved to shield its elections from federal interference.

stories.title: Houthis claim missile and drone strikes on Riyadh, flames seen near airport
stories.why_it_matters: Yemen's Houthi rebel group launched what it claimed were missile and drone strikes on Riyadh, Saudi Arabia's capital — with thick smoke and flames reported near the main airport. This is a major escalation; Riyadh is rarely directly targeted. The strike likely contributed to oil market volatility, though crude actually fell sharply as traders weighed demand fears against supply disruption risk. For everyday Australians, continued Middle East instability keeps energy costs unpredictable.

stories.title: Pakistan risks being dragged into Middle East conflict via Saudi pact
stories.why_it_matters: A defence agreement between Pakistan and Saudi Arabia is raising fears that Pakistan — a nuclear-armed nation — could be pulled into the widening Middle East conflict. If Saudi Arabia calls on Pakistan for military support in response to Houthi attacks, it could dramatically widen the scope of the war. This is one to watch closely: a broader regional conflict involving nuclear powers would shake global markets hard.

stories.title: World leaders gather at UN General Assembly amid wars in Middle East and Ukraine
stories.why_it_matters: The UN General Assembly is underway in New York, with heads of state from across the world gathering to address the conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East. These meetings rarely produce immediate breakthroughs, but they set the diplomatic tone for the months ahead — including whether ceasefire talks in either conflict gain any traction. Geopolitical uncertainty at this level keeps global markets on edge.

stories.title: California governor signs laws to block federal election interference
stories.why_it_matters: California Governor Gavin Newsom has signed a package of election security laws specifically designed to prevent the Trump administration from interfering in the state's elections. This is part of a broader and intensifying legal battle between California and the federal government. It reflects deep divisions in US governance that could affect everything from tech regulation (important for your GOOGL and MSFT holdings) to trade policy.

markets.summary: Last night was broadly positive for US markets — the S&P 500 and NASDAQ both nudged higher. The big story was oil, which cratered nearly 6% after Houthi attacks on Riyadh paradoxically failed to lift prices as demand fears dominated. Gold hit a new high near $4,425. The ASX was dead flat today, essentially unchanged.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Flat as a tack today — the ASX barely moved, closing almost exactly where it started.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Modest gains last night — markets shrugged off Middle East noise and crept higher.

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicators.note: Tech led the way last night with a 0.4% gain, helping your GOOGL and VTS holdings.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Massive drop — oil fell nearly 6% despite Houthi attacks on Riyadh. Demand fears are winning over supply concerns right now.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Gold pushed higher again, near all-time highs. Investors are seeking safety amid global uncertainty.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: The Aussie dollar was barely changed — sitting just above 71 US cents.

politics.summary: Two big domestic stories this weekend: the RBA looks set to keep hiking interest rates, and PM Albanese is pushing hard for international AI regulation after meeting with Tim Cook.

stories.title: Traders now pricing in three more RBA rate rises — ASX sell-off expected to resume
stories.why_it_matters: Financial markets are now pricing in three more rate rises from the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) — meaning the cost of mortgages and business loans could keep climbing. The AFR reports the ASX is expected to resume a sell-off as investors digest this. Higher rates hurt growth stocks and property-linked shares most. For everyday Aussies with mortgages, this means more pain at the repayment table in the months ahead.

stories.title: Albanese backs stronger AI regulation after Tim Cook meeting, seeks global coalition
stories.why_it_matters: Prime Minister Albanese met with Apple CEO Tim Cook and is now actively pushing for an international coalition to regulate AI — positioning Australia alongside the EU and against the Trump administration's anti-regulation stance. Albanese wants binding guardrails on AI development and has reached out to tech industry leaders for support. This could lead to new laws affecting how AI is used by Australian businesses and consumers, and signals Australia won't be a regulatory free-for-all for big tech.

ai.summary: The week's biggest AI story is a major antitrust lawsuit accusing Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, and Elon Musk's xAI of secretly agreeing to slow down AI development — an allegation all companies deny. Also: Australia is pushing for global AI guardrails.

stories.title: Lawsuit accuses Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and SpaceXAI of illegal deal to slow AI
stories.why_it_matters: A new lawsuit filed in the US alleges that the four biggest AI labs — Anthropic, OpenAI, Google's DeepMind, and Elon Musk's xAI — secretly agreed to 'pace' (deliberately slow down) AI development, which would be an illegal anti-competitive arrangement similar to a cartel. The companies deny it, saying their public discussions about AI safety are legitimate. If the allegations have merit, it could mean massive fines and forced restructuring for the companies involved — including Google, which you hold. The case is also ironic: critics usually worry about AI going too fast, not that companies are colluding to slow it down.

stories.title: Australia pushes for big tech cooperation on AI regulation and internet safety
stories.why_it_matters: Australia is seeking big tech's cooperation in regulating AI and improving internet safety, with PM Albanese meeting tech executives including Apple's Tim Cook. The government wants global coordination so Australia isn't left setting rules alone — a sensible approach given how borderless AI is. For investors in AI-exposed stocks like GOOGL and GXAI, more regulation generally means compliance costs but also more certainty and legitimacy for the industry long-term.

stories.title: GPT Store vs Claude Skills vs Gemini Gems: The AI assistant marketplace war heats up
stories.why_it_matters: A new analysis compares the three main AI assistant marketplaces: OpenAI's GPT Store, Anthropic's Claude Skills, and Google's Gemini Gems — with a reported 159,000-unit gap between the leader and the others. These are the 'app stores' for AI tools, where developers build specialised assistants for everything from legal research to coding help. The size of these ecosystems matters for long-term platform dominance — and Google's position here is directly relevant to your GOOGL holding.

sport.summary: It's NRL Finals Week 2 — the Roosters demolished the Sharks last night, and the Warriors vs Knights is live right now. In AFL, Brisbane Lions beat Hawthorn in a classic preliminary final, though the aftermath has stirred controversy.

stories.title: Roosters thrash Sharks 46-10 in Finals Week 2 demolition
stories.why_it_matters: The Sydney Roosters put on a masterclass at Allianz Stadium last night, hammering the Cronulla Sharks 46-10 in what was a one-sided Finals Week 2 clash. A 36-point margin is emphatic — the Roosters look genuinely dangerous heading deeper into the finals. The Sharks, by contrast, are out of the competition.

stories.title: Warriors vs Knights — live in 2nd half at Eden Park
stories.why_it_matters: The Warriors are hosting the Newcastle Knights at Eden Park right now — it's currently the 2nd half with the Knights leading 12-6. The Warriors had a double injury boost heading in (late mail suggested key players were cleared to play), but the Knights are hanging tough. Still anyone's game — check the score live.

stories.title: Brisbane Lions beat Hawthorn in AFL preliminary final classic — but controversy follows
stories.why_it_matters: Brisbane Lions defeated Hawthorn in what's being described as one of the greatest preliminary finals ever played, booking their spot in the AFL Grand Final. However the aftermath turned ugly — Lions players were accused of a 'classless' act immediately after the final siren, and the AFL is now investigating after umpires were targeted in unsavoury post-match scenes, with the league vowing major punishment. The Hawks coaching staff also reportedly received a blunt reality check from a Lions official.

stories.title: AFL Grand Final preview: Penelope van Lith (PVL) and the $5m payday problem
stories.why_it_matters: With the AFL Grand Final looming, The Australian reports on what's standing between star player Penelope van Lith (PVL) and a potential $5 million payday — with a 'glaring problem' identified that could derail her biggest earnings opportunity. No article text was available, but it's shaping up as one of the big pre-Grand Final storylines worth following this week.
